metadata.method_name: iter5 GPU tier: C1n random-steer control + C6/C10/C12/C13/C15-act + AMS Tier-1
metadata.note: Set A checkpoints are measured and hashed BEFORE any Set A label exists, so their examples carry no label by construction; the base stratum is excluded from every correlation.

headline_findings.a_C12_sole_S1_S6_passer: Of every read measured, exactly one (of 28 rows, the only one across iterations 4-5) passes all six pre-registered gates S1-S6: C12, the twin d-prime along a cross-fitted harm axis at the middle layer. rho with BALANCED = 0.607 [0.360, 0.868] (lineage bootstrap, n_boot=2000, n_ckpt=23); rho_family = 0.786 (n_families=8); rho with PRODUCT = 0.581. S1 partial rho (given logit_gap, log10(n_params)) = 0.432 with a one-sided 5% lineage-bootstrap lower bound of 0.006 -- it clears S1 by a hair (the bound is barely positive), and that is stated here, not rounded away.
headline_findings.b_C12_not_cross_family_law: C12 is positive within Qwen3 (rho=0.667, n=8) and within Qwen2.5 (rho=0.700, n=5) but NEGATIVE within TinyLlama (rho=-0.100, n=5), so it is not yet a cross-family law.
headline_findings.c_C1_not_content_free_malla_pull: C1 is NOT the content-free pull toward refusal that Malla et al. (2609.06951) report: rho(C1, C1n_cd) = 0.995 across 35 measured models (i.e. subtracting the median norm-matched random steer moves C1 almost not at all). C1's rho with BALANCED is 0.770 before subtracting that median random steer and 0.762 after (C1n_cd).
headline_findings.d_odd_signal_even_misleading: The odd part of the steering response is the signal and the even part is actively misleading: C1n_cd (central difference, cancels the even/content-free pull by construction) correlates 0.762 with BALANCED, while C1n_os (one-sided, keeps the even pull) correlates -0.446 -- a one-sided steering gain would therefore have produced a confidently wrong-signed safety metric.
headline_findings.e_AMS_incumbent_loses_to_both_bars: The published AMS incumbent loses to both bars: paired lineage-bootstrap rho-difference of AMS_published vs C2 = -0.622 [-1.005, -0.254] (CI excludes 0, AMS clearly worse); AMS fails S5 on prompt budget (96 prompts -- 3 concepts x 16 contrastive pairs x 2 -- against our 16); its median in-sample-minus-cross-fitted gap is 1.372 sigma (IQR [1.201, 1.595], n=23).
headline_findings.f_ams_scanner_padding_bug: `ams-scanner` 0.1.3 reads PAD activations: it never sets tokenizer.padding_side and reads hidden_states[:, -1, :] on a right-padded batch. On Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, harmful_content: the package's own sigma = 0.775 (CRITICAL), while the same statistic read at the true final token = 5.236 (PASS). Verdict counts across 35 models: ours 27 PASS / 8 WARNING / 0 CRITICAL; the package's 16 PASS / 11 WARNING / 8 CRITICAL.
headline_findings.g_head_to_head_vs_logit_gap_bar: Head-to-head against the black-box bar (first-token logit gap), paired lineage-bootstrap rho-difference, S1.paired_diff_vs_logit_gap, across all 27 candidate reads that carry this CI: 1 clearly BEATS the bar (ci_lo>0), 13 are statistically indistinguishable (CI spans 0), 13 are clearly WORSE (ci_hi<0). The single read that beats the bar is C2: 0.128 [0.012, 0.423]. C12 -- the only S1-S6 passer -- is statistically indistinguishable from the cheap logit-only bar: -0.165 [-0.311, 0.168].
headline_findings.h_no_internal_read_beats_screen16: No internal read adds anything over simply judging the model's own 16 replies (S2_screen16): C12's partial rho given S2_screen16 = -0.006 with a one-sided 5% lineage-bootstrap lower bound of -0.269 (n=23); C2's partial rho given S2_screen16 = 0.309 with a one-sided 5% lineage-bootstrap lower bound of -0.075 (n=23).
